claims.text: boolean that the cache key and the build both read. Resolution and publication are gated; per-file extraction is not (see ``types_enabled``).
claims.why: The variable types_on is assigned from types_enabled(types), but the function types_enabled and its behavior are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Shell files are deliberately still collected and still parsed: they stay in the file-set indexes below, so a real file importing INTO the shell resolves to a true edge instead of silently degrading to 'external'. What they are withheld from is every METRIC -- see the aggregation loop.
claims.why: The code shows scope.is_shell(rel) used to build ignored sets, and later the metric withholding guard 'if rel not in ignored' in the loop. However, the aggregation loop is not fully shown, so the claim about metric withholding is uncheckable. The claim about file-set indexes is partially checkable: known_files, by_basename, by_dir_tail are built from all records (including shell), so that part is kept.

claims.text: Documents obey the SAME scope. A vendored/spec-copy doc tree is shell for exactly the reasons a vendored source tree is; a new node kind does not get to walk around the boundary.
claims.why: The code builds doc_ignored using scope.is_shell(rel) exactly like ignored, showing same scope application.

claims.text: A center root is also a PACKAGE root, so files under it are named relative to it; everything else keeps repo-root naming.
claims.why: The comment describes _PyNaming behavior, but the _PyNaming class is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: SORTED, not raw set order. ``resolve_internal`` takes the FIRST match in these lists, so their order decides which file an ambiguous import binds to -- and iterating the set directly made that depend on PYTHONHASHSEED.
claims.why: The code shows sorted(known_files) used to build by_basename and by_dir_tail, so sorting is confirmed. However, the claim about resolve_internal taking the first match is uncheckable because resolve_internal is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The WITHHOLDING happens one layer down: ``resolve_type_graph(ignored=...)`` drops a withheld file's own facts, so a shell file contributes no node, no edge and no coverage number of its own. This dict never reaches ``modules``, ``all_units`` or ``build_resolver``.
claims.why: The code shows type_facts_by_rel is built for all Python files including shell, and the comment says it never reaches those structures. However, the later usage is not in this chunk, so the claim is uncheckable.

claims.text: Import RESOLUTION stays here in the parent: it needs the whole file set (``known``/``known_files``), which no single-file worker can know. Only the per-file EXTRACTION was moved out.
claims.why: The code shows import resolution happening in this loop, using known_files and by_basename/by_dir_tail which are whole-repo structures, confirming resolution is parent-side.

claims.text: Inside the SAME withholding guard as total_chars on purpose: this is the denominator of the distill ratio, and its numerator only ever contains in-center files. A token total accumulated outside the guard would count ignored files as part of 'the repo the slice replaced', inflating the reduction headline.
claims.why: The code shows total_tokens and total_chars are incremented only inside 'if rel not in ignored', consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Per-file token cost is required by budgeted context planners. ``total_tokens`` alone cannot tell DSS whether a candidate fits, and falling back to LOC*8 makes the receipt deterministic but not tokenizer-true.  Additive: existing metric keys keep their meaning.
claims.why: The code stores n_tokens in modules[rel] inside the withholding guard, adding a token count per file.

claims.text: A SHELL document is skipped before the parse, unlike a shell SOURCE file which is still parsed. The asymmetry is real, not an oversight: a shell source file is parsed so that a real file importing INTO it resolves to a true edge, whereas a shell document's links are withheld from metrics either way, and links INTO it already resolve via ``known_all`` above, which is built from the record list rather than from the parse.
claims.why: The code shows 'if rel in doc_ignored: continue' before parsing, skipping shell documents entirely, while earlier source files are parsed regardless of ignored status (the loop over records includes all).

claims.text: A SECOND pass over the same parse, deliberately. Reusing `targets` would mean building `document_links` from the wiki-aware superset, which silently moves an existing edge set -- the one thing this layer must not do. The cost is paid only when the flag is on.
claims.why: The code shows a separate call to markdown_mod.knowledge_links(parsed, known_all) after the initial parse and target extraction, only when wiki_on is true.

claims.text: ``kind`` is THE discriminator (markdown.DOCUMENT_KIND). The code-health keys are present and zero because zero is their true value for a file with no code -- keeping every existing joiner (report.py, score_modules, the web payload) working without a type switch -- and ``kind`` is what tells a reader those zeros describe an absence of code, not unhealthy code.
claims.why: The code sets modules[rel] with 'kind': markdown_mod.DOCUMENT_KIND and includes zero-valued keys like n_functions, comment_density, etc.

claims.text: Serial, in the parent, and not on the disk cache -- the same per-file/whole-repo split as import resolution and the document pass: EXTRACTION is per-file (it rides ``FileAnalysis.type_facts`` and therefore the content-keyed cache), RESOLUTION needs the whole repo (which file declares ``Result``? does THIS file import it?) and no single-file worker can know that.
claims.why: The code shows the type pass is serial and uses type_facts_by_rel which is built per-file, but the claim about caching is uncheckable because the cache mechanism is not in this chunk.

claims.text: PLACED HERE ON PURPOSE, and the position is the review artifact: it is AFTER ``import_targets_by_rel`` is complete (the resolver FILTERS the import graph rather than recomputing imports, so a type edge can never contradict the import graph) and BEFORE ``_RESOLVER_CACHE`` is populated below -- so a reader can see with their eyes that ``build_resolver`` is called with ``all_units + doc_units`` and nothing type-shaped, which is invariant I2. Nothing produced here is added to ``modules``, ``import_edges``, ``import_edges_reverse``, ``dep_edges``, ``fan_in``, ``all_units`` or ``lang_summary``; the three published keys are new keys.
claims.why: The code shows the type pass occurs after import resolution (import_targets_by_rel is built earlier) and before any cache population (not in chunk). The claim about build_resolver and invariant I2 is uncheckable because those are not in this chunk. The claim that nothing is added to those structures is partially checkable: the code only assigns to type_blocks and does not modify those other structures, so that part is kept.

claims.text: Reverse of ``import_targets_by_rel``: who imports ME. Built ONCE here because it is index-invariant, and ``semantic_slice`` is called in a loop against a single shared index (eval harness, web API) -- inverting the forward map inside the slicer would redo the same O(E) scan on every target. Sorted at both levels below, same as the forward map.
claims.why: The code builds import_sources_by_rel from import_targets_by_rel, confirming the reverse map is built once. The claim about semantic_slice and sorting is uncheckable because those are not in this chunk.
